items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: A girl named Laura played piano for me. ... I had my own pianist; a girl named Laura played for me out in vaudeville

ctx.x: You went on tour with that show, didn't you?

Oh, yeah. We toured the -- like Baltimore and all those. Then after I came back from the show, I toured by myself, just with a pianist and a dancer. The girl that played piano for -- no, that was before Pearl's time. A girl named Laura played piano for me. And Leroy Bloomfield was my dancer. And we played all the different houses, Washington, Baltimore, and all down that way. And then I got work in the big White Theaters. Like the Keith Houses, and all.

items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: I had my own pianist; a girl named Laura played for me out in vaudeville when I was playing the big white houses, Laura.

ctx.x: Yeah. Had a band. Had a band, but he'd go as a pianist, too. And then there was -- let me see, did I buy my place on 138th Street? Yes. When I left 287 Edgecomb I bought my place on 138th Street, 133 West 138th Street.
